scope: Public anchors for an engineering estimate; not a quote, invoice, or project measurement.

sources.title: Transportation Economic Trends: Transportation Spending - Per Vehicle Mile
sources.evidence: The 2024 year-in-review reports an average cost of owning and operating a new vehicle of about $0.82 per mile at 15,000 miles per year.
sources.boundary: Consumer vehicle ownership cost; it excludes ADS sensors, safety operator, test engineer, proving ground, insurance uplift, and data operations.

sources.title: Your Driving Costs 2024 fact sheet
sources.evidence: AAA reports an overall average cost to own and operate a new car in 2024 of $12,297, with a sales-weighted average MSRP of $38,883; the study uses five top-selling models in each of nine categories.
sources.use_in_model: Cross-check for the BTS per-mile anchor and vehicle depreciation/ownership component.
sources.boundary: New-car consumer ownership study, not instrumented AV fleet operating cost.

sources.title: Automotive Service Technicians and Mechanics
sources.evidence: The May 2024 median annual wage is $49,670.
sources.use_in_model: Lower-bound labor anchor for a safety operator or vehicle technician; converted from annual wage using 2,080 hours/year and an explicit burden multiplier.
sources.boundary: U.S. occupational median wage; local wage, overtime, contractor markup, and employer burden vary.

sources.title: Software Developers, Quality Assurance Analysts, and Testers
sources.evidence: The May 2024 median annual wage for software developers is $133,080.
sources.use_in_model: Test-engineer allocation anchor; only a fractional allocation is charged to one test run.
sources.boundary: U.S. occupational median wage, not an AV test engineer quote.

sources.title: Driving to Safety: How Many Miles of Driving Would It Take to Demonstrate Autonomous Vehicle Reliability?
sources.evidence: The report estimates hundreds of millions to hundreds of billions of miles may be required for statistical safety evidence. One example uses 275 million failure-free miles and a 100-vehicle fleet at 25 mph, taking about 12.5 years; estimating a low failure rate to 20% precision is shown as about 8.8 billion miles and about 400 years for the same fleet.
sources.use_in_model: Evidence for why rare-event real-road campaigns are expensive and why simulation is useful for candidate discovery.
sources.boundary: Statistical feasibility analysis, not a per-mile price and not a claim about this project's safety.

sources.title: Simulated terrible drivers cut the time and cost of AV testing by a factor of one thousand
sources.evidence: The mixed-reality research reports a 1,000-fold reduction in testing time/cost for its rare-event evaluation setup and a 99.99% reduction in required testing miles.
sources.use_in_model: External opportunity bound showing that targeted simulation can dominate rare-event real-road sampling.
sources.boundary: Specific mixed-reality system and study design; cannot be transferred as the measured result of this CARLA project.
